name: Complex analysis: the plane of numbers
description: Complex numbers, analytic functions, contour integrals, series and residues, taught at the Kepler outpost's Wave Station.
about:
Complex analysis realm ("Complex analysis: the plane of numbers"): complex numbers, analytic functions, contour integrals,
Cauchy's formulas, series and residues, for an adult who has finished Foundations, Calculus 1 and 2, Logic and proof, and
Real analysis. Same Kepler outpost, now working in the plane of numbers, and Mira is still the mentor. Angles are in radians.
The concept plan is docs/plans/COMPLEX-PLAN.md.

chapters.name: Complex numbers
chapters.blurb: The number i, arithmetic, the complex plane, polar form, powers and roots.

sector.name: Antenna Field
sector.purpose: describe every signal with one number

chapters.name: Exponentials and logarithms
chapters.blurb: Functions as maps, the complex exponential, logarithms and powers.

sector.name: Rotor Hall
sector.purpose: keep track of everything that turns

chapters.name: Analytic functions
chapters.blurb: The complex derivative, Cauchy–Riemann, trigonometric functions and harmonic functions.

sector.name: Flow Tank
sector.purpose: model smooth flow round the hull

chapters.name: Contour integrals
chapters.blurb: Integrals along curves, antiderivatives, Cauchy's theorem and winding numbers.

sector.name: Ring Road
sector.purpose: add up a field all the way round a loop

chapters.name: Cauchy's formula
chapters.blurb: Cauchy's integral formula, derivatives, bounds, mean values and maximum modulus.

sector.name: Field Lab
sector.purpose: read the inside of a region from its edge

chapters.name: Series
chapters.blurb: Geometric and power series, Taylor and Laurent series, poles.

sector.name: Signal Archive
sector.purpose: build any signal out of simple powers

chapters.name: Residues
chapters.blurb: Residues, the residue theorem, real integrals and the argument principle.

sector.name: Control Room
sector.purpose: turn hard integrals into quick sums

mentor.name: Mira
mentor.opening: I’m Mira. Nothing out here is a single line any more, and we have to {purpose}. Your task is “{title}.” {brief} The idea we need: {topic}.
mentor.closing: You already have the derivatives and integrals from Calculus 1 and 2. I’ll go through the worked example with you, and the guided steps are there whenever you want them.

copy.homeEyebrow: THE SIGNALS NOW HAVE TWO PARTS
copy.homeTitle:
Every point is a number.
Learn to calculate in the plane.
copy.firstVisit: Welcome to the Wave Station. Our antennas turn signals round and round, and the cleanest way to track a turn is with a number that has two parts. We start with the strange new number i.
copy.allDone: You can now turn any integral round a loop into a sum of residues. Waves opens next at the Antenna Field, where these turning numbers ride on every signal.
copy.chaptersNote: Seven chapters. Learn every concept in a chapter to unlock a landmark for the outpost. Practice missions are optional.

skills.title: The skill tree
skills.text: Follow the prerequisite branches from the number i to the residue theorem. Each mission you finish opens the ideas that are built on it.

visual.title: The concept bench
visual.text: Pick any mission, change its numbers and predict the result before you check it. Nothing here affects your progress, and it all works offline.

help.title: Every point is a number.
help.intro: Complex analysis starts from the number i and the plane that holds every complex number. It then adds exponentials and logarithms, analytic functions, contour integrals, Cauchy's formulas, series and residues. Every new word and symbol is explained before you are asked to use it, with a worked example first.
help.answers: A complex answer is typed as its real part and its imaginary part in two boxes; angles are in radians, and a count, an order or a winding number is a whole number.
